Specifically: would you recommend adding a fixed number of "hours" on Dedicated or swapping to a credit pack we can consume? We want a predictable top-up that aligns to a 2-week timebox. Also, any impact to the pilot terms if we add a brief extension?

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on extending the eval window

Jordan — thanks for the note. Short answer: we can do either, but the two options trade off predictability vs price. High level options: 

1) Timebox hours (Dedicated burst allocation): we reserve N hours of dedicated capacity for two weeks. Predictable latency and simpler to schedule your tests. Priced at hourly rate; this is easiest if your tests require steady concurrency and low p95 latency.

2) Credit pack (flex credits): you prepay a token/credit pool that the test draws from. More cost-efficient if usage is spiky because automatic batching and KV caching reduce per-token cost. Slightly less predictable in raw hours but better unit economics for bursty workloads.

3) Hybrid short-bridge: small dedicated buffer + credits for peak bursts. Gives you baseline latency SLA through the buffer and cheaper credits for spikes.

If you want an official amendment for a 2-week extension, we can do a short SOW addendum (no changes to core pilot terms). I've attached a draft SOW showing the three options and a sample usage snapshot from your trial so we can size the offers.

Which option sounds closest to your tests? I can propose exact numbers once we pick the model.

Thanks,
David

--
David Kim
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
